problem: Express $\frac{5{x}^{2}+2x+5}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)(x-1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.

feedback.problem: Express $\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{C}{(x-11)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-43x-20=(Ax+B)(x-11)+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=11$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(11)^{2}-43(11)-20 & =(A(11)+B)(11-11)+C((11)^{2}+3) \\ 121-473-20 & =124C \\ -372 & =124C \\ C & =-\frac{372}{124} \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}-43(0)-20 & =(A(0)+B)(0-11)+C({0}^{2}+3) \\ -20 & =-11B+3C \\ -20 & =-11B+3(-3) \\ 11B & =-9+20 \\ B & =\frac{11}{11} \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}-43(1)-20 & =(A(1)+B)(1-11)+C({1}^{2}+3) \\ -62 & =-10A-10B+4C \\ -62 & =-10A-10(1)+4(-3) \\ 10A & =-10-12+62 \\ A & =\frac{40}{10} \\ A & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=4,$ $B=1,$ and $C=-3.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)}=\frac{4x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)}-\frac{3}{(x-11)}.
$$
